text:
Ada: Heads up — packing efficiency dropped ~12% on Saturday afternoon in us-west when we saw mixed H100/A100 load. Lots of 0.25-slot fragments showing up. Anyone else notice?
capacity-bot: [auto] fragmentation_ratio=0.27 active_pools=34 tail_latency_p99=420ms (snapshot 2026-03-14T18:02Z)
Sam (oncall): Yup, saw it in the alerts. Most evictions were tiny 0.25-slot leftover chunks. The scheduler currently prefers strict same-type binpack which creates those holes.
Priya: We should try a hetero-fit heuristic — allow different GPU types to co-reside when constraints (mem, batch) permit. Also consider dynamic slice resizing during low-util periods.
Miguel: Quick sim run showed hetero-fit + soft-evict reduces frag from .27 -> .15 but increases p95 by ~12ms. Seems promising as a cost/throughput trade.
Ada: Can you paste the sim command and a short summary? Need to run across APAC windows too.
Miguel: ```
# sim command
./sim --workload weekend_peak.json --policy hetero-fit --soft-evict --warm-pool 5% --regions us-west,ap-southeast --output brief

# summary
packing_util_mean: 0.82
fragmentation_ratio: 0.15
p95_latency_ms: 120 (+12ms)
cost_delta: -9%
```
Priya: Also add a 90-minute prewarm for the expected surge window; a low-cost warm pool with <1% reserved capacity can smooth the initial burst without big commit.
Sam (oncall): Main concern is reserved cost vs evict churn. For the forecasted surge we estimate ~18k GPU-hours current config vs ~16.2k with hetero-fit + prewarm (so ~10% GPU-hour savings).
Ada: Let's schedule a small canary. Run hetero-fit on 10% of nodes in us-west and ap-southeast during next Friday's 18:00-22:00 window. Rollback if p99 > 500ms or fragmentation_ratio increases.
capacity-bot: Canary scheduled: policy=hetero-fit sample=10% windows=[2026-03-20T18:00Z-2026-03-20T22:00Z] monitor=[fragmentation_ratio,p99_latency,eviction_rate]
Priya: I'll open the RFC with config flags, rollout plan, and target metrics: fragmentation_ratio, packing_util_{95,mean}, eviction_count_per_hour, p99_latency, cost_delta.
Sam (oncall): sgtm. I'll draft an ops rollback runbook and watch thresholds. @Miguel can you add sim configs to the experiment repo?
Miguel: Done — pushed config and results to experiments/slot-fit/1999-hetero. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/experiments/slot-fit/1999-hetero :rocket:
Ada: :thumbsup: Heads-up to infra oncall rotation and capacity planning. We'll review after the canary window and decide on global rollout.
